dataset_refs: eight fresh unexposed public development identities admitted by sealed scoreability
experiment_template.research_question: Can exact pre-dispatch upper-bound debits and symmetric pair censoring preserve token safety while allowing a fresh GLM 8K ContextBench cohort to produce an interpretable H62 estimate?
stop_conditions: Any unbounded unknown usage, retry, asymmetric score, integrity failure, or cost-cap violation stops before the next task.

records.falsifier: Any indeterminate call lacks a complete bound, any retry occurs, any affected pair is scored asymmetrically, fewer than six pairs complete, or all eight task outcomes are not accounted.
records.mechanism: Validate the terminal receipt, dispatch and admission as one bound chain; debit the full projected request; score both arms zero for the affected task; continue only later independent tasks.
records.scope: GLM-5.3-flash fresh scoreable 8K ContextBench development tasks at the 96K cumulative input-plus-output tier.
records.statement: Conservative debit of narrowly proven indeterminate calls plus symmetric pair censoring allows independent ContextBench tasks to continue without understating token use or favoring an arm.

selection.reason: Rounds 40 and 41 independently reached 300-second and 900-second zero-byte provider deadlines. Round 41 still had an exact admitted 3,736-token request upper bound, so the global stop is now the instrument bottleneck. H62 remains the unchanged semantic comparison inside this harness experiment.
